newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds steadily recouped initial losses on Monday to end slightly higher as the long-term uptrend continued, traders said.
"In the longer term, we are expecting a climb, particularly at the long end (of the curve)," one trader said.
Longer dated paper did indeed gain most.
However, thin volumes and the lack of U.S. players left a number of traders regarding the gains as inconclusive. A public holiday in the U.S. sidelined treasuries.
"It just shows that if they're not there, it's just a disaster," one trader said.
In a low-key day, traded volume of 1999 paper was at least respectable in the morning. Traders said some players were encouraged to buy at the mild dip.
Some players also took an interest in medium-dated paper, with maturities from 2000 to 2002, from mid-session, traders said.
Spreads under German bunds remained virtually unchanged after initial underperformance of Dutch bonds.
